issue.body:
### Description

`StreamExecutorGpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()` (`xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_topology_description.cc`) hashes the deterministic serialization of the client's `GpuTopologyProto`. That proto embeds `gpu_target_config.gpu_device_info` for one local device, including `device_interconnect_info` (`GpuDeviceInfoProto` field 29: `active_links`, `cluster_uuid`, `clique_id`). `cuda_executor.cc` reads it from NVML for each device. So the fingerprint isn't a property of the job's topology: it depends on which GPU is the process's first device.

On one host with 4x RTX 3090 (GPU0-GPU1 NV4, GPU2-GPU3 PHB, cross-pair SYS), a job of four processes, one GPU each, builds the same global topology in every process: 4 devices, 4 processes. Yet processes on GPU0 and GPU1 get one fingerprint, and processes on GPU2 and GPU3 get another. Decoding each process's topology proto shows that one field differs: `gpu_target_config.gpu_device_info.device_interconnect_info.active_links` is 4 on GPU0 and GPU1 and absent on GPU2 and GPU3 (`topology-diff.txt` below). `Serialize()` isn't canonical either: map entries come out in a different order in every process, although `Fingerprint()` serializes deterministically.

### Why it matters

JAX keys its persistent compilation cache by this fingerprint (`jax/_src/cache_key.py`, `_hash_accelerator_config`, since #39387). XLA's compile of a program that spans processes shards autotuning over them (`ConfigAssignerPass` with the compile's `MultiProcessKeyValueStore`), and each process waits for the others' shares. With keys that differ between the processes of one job, some processes load a cached executable while the others compile, and those compiles wait forever for shares that never come: jax-ml/jax#40940. JAX can avoid this by hashing the fingerprints of all the processes a computation spans, as proposed there (branch `cache-key-pool-fingerprints` on AshishKumar4/jax). Anything else that uses `Fingerprint()` as a job-wide identity has the same problem.

Even with that fix, a program on one process's devices keeps that process's fingerprint. In a four-process training job on this host, the processes on GPU2 and GPU3 recompile their one-process programs on every run, because only process 0 writes the cache and their fingerprint differs from its. A one-device program reads no link at all.

### Questions

1. Should the topology fingerprint of a multi-process client describe the job rather than one local device? The client already exchanges local topologies when it's created (the key-value exchange that builds the global topology). A fingerprint over every device's description would be the same in every process.

2. Should per-device link info be in a key for a program that spans processes? At openxla/xla@91888df6 (jax 0.11.2), `active_links` reaches compilation in three places:
   - `SolLatencyEstimator`, used only on Hopper, Blackwell and MI300 (`IsSupportedForModule`);
   - the analytical latency estimator (`gpu_collective_performance_model.cc`), behind `xla_gpu_enable_analytical_latency_estimator`, which is off by default;
   - the collective kernels (`all_reduce.cc`, `all_gather.cc`), which need NVLink and replicas all local to one process, which a multi-process program never has.

   #40177 made `GpuTargetConfig` device-agnostic for exactly this reason: fields unique to one GPU, the PCI bus ID and the NVLink UUIDs, made the configs of two GPUs of one model differ, "which is a problem when used as a cache key". It left `active_links`, which is now the one field that differs here. #49099 (`openxla/xla@86ee39e615`) normalizes `device_memory_size` and clears `model_str` for the same portability. `active_links` can't simply be dropped, since a single-process program's collective kernels and SOL estimates read it. But a program that spans processes doesn't read it at this revision, so a fingerprint that describes the job, or a link count taken as the job's minimum, would keep one key per job.

3. The target config describes only one device of a process. A single process that owns GPUs with different links (all four GPUs of this host) compiles every program with its first device's `active_links`, including a program that runs on GPU2 and GPU3 alone. Is that intended?

### Evidence

<details><summary>topology-diff.txt: each rank's decoded topology proto and the one differing field</summary>

```
Raw-protobuf decode of xla_client.get_topology_for_devices(jax.devices()).serialize() in each process of a
four-process pool (dew launch 4x1) on the 4x RTX 3090 box (GPU0-GPU1 NV4, GPU2-GPU3 PHB, cross-socket SYS), jax 0.11.2:
  rank 0 (GPU0): 766 bytes, 80 fields    rank 1 (GPU1): 766 bytes, 80 fields
  rank 2 (GPU2): 761 bytes, 79 fields    rank 3 (GPU3): 761 bytes, 79 fields
As field sets, ranks 0 and 1 are identical and ranks 2 and 3 are identical. The one difference:
  field path /9/2/8/1/29/1 = 4 on ranks 0 and 1, absent on ranks 2 and 3
  (inside the embedded GpuTopologyProto's device description; 4 matches the NV4 link count between GPU0 and GPU1).
The serialized bytes also list a repeated/map field's entries in a different order in every process
(rank 0 and rank 1 differ in order only), so serialize() is not canonical either.
JAX's cache key hashes topology.fingerprint() (jax/_src/cache_key.py _hash_accelerator_config); in the same pool
its component hash was d8852249... on ranks 0,1 and 8b8b9014... on ranks 2,3 for one 4-device SPMD jit
(computation, compile_options, XLA flags and backend version hashes identical on all ranks).
In a single process the four devices give one accelerator_config hash (dc2d2ee7...).
```
</details>

<details><summary>JAX's cache-key components for one four-process SPMD program, first 12 hex digits of each component's hash (DEBUG log of jax._src.cache_key, jax 0.11.2)</summary>

```
component          rank 0 (GPU0)  rank 1 (GPU1)  rank 2 (GPU2)  rank 3 (GPU3)
computation        88c32b69db78   88c32b69db78   88c32b69db78   88c32b69db78 
jax_lib version    7558e7d2c821   7558e7d2c821   7558e7d2c821   7558e7d2c821 
backend version    a224da3101c0   a224da3101c0   a224da3101c0   a224da3101c0 
XLA flags          e3b0c44298fc   e3b0c44298fc   e3b0c44298fc   e3b0c44298fc 
compile_options    b47e2d3afdb0   b47e2d3afdb0   b47e2d3afdb0   b47e2d3afdb0 
accelerator_config d8852249e57e   d8852249e57e   8b8b901463e0   8b8b901463e0 
compression        0ea55c28f801   0ea55c28f801   0ea55c28f801   0ea55c28f801 
custom_hook        e3b0c44298fc   e3b0c44298fc   e3b0c44298fc   e3b0c44298fc 
```

Only the accelerator config differs, between ranks 0,1 and ranks 2,3.
</details>

### System info

- jax 0.11.2 and jaxlib 0.11.2 (jax-cuda12-plugin), XLA 91888df6ce85102c30220e41d952065925e10886
- 4x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, driver 595.84, one host. `nvidia-smi topo -m`: GPU0-GPU1 NV4, GPU2-GPU3 PHB, cross-pair SYS
issue.title: [GPU] The topology fingerprint is process-local: it hashes one local device's interconnect info, so the processes of one job fingerprint the same topology differently

issue.body:
### Description

On a host where only some GPUs are joined by NVLink, the processes of one multi-process job (one process per GPU) compute different persistent compilation cache keys for the same program that spans them. Process 0 is the only one that writes the cache. So on the next run, the processes whose GPU has process 0's NVLink link count load the executable, and the others miss and compile. A rank that compiles while its peers loaded then waits forever in XLA's sharded autotuning for shares nobody sends, and the peers wait in the program's collectives. The whole job hangs.

**1. The key embeds the process's own GPU's NVLink link count.** `_hash_accelerator_config` (`jax/_src/cache_key.py`) hashes `xla_client.get_topology_for_devices(devices).fingerprint()`, and for a GPU that is `StreamExecutorGpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()`. The fingerprinted proto includes the local device's `gpu_target_config.gpu_device_info`, whose `device_interconnect_info` (field 29) carries `active_links`, the NVLink link count read through NVML. openxla/xla#40177 made the target config device-agnostic by removing the PCI bus ID and NVLink UUIDs, but `active_links` stays.

On 4x RTX 3090 (GPU0-GPU1 NV4, GPU2-GPU3 PHB), decoding each process's topology proto shows one difference: `active_links = 4` on GPU0 and GPU1, absent on GPU2 and GPU3. The processes on GPU0 and GPU1 fingerprint alike, as do those on GPU2 and GPU3, and the two pairs differ. For one 4-process SPMD program, the computation, compile options, flags and backend hash the same on every rank, and only the accelerator-config component differs between the pairs. The GPU cache key already strips the device assignment "to use cache key as invariant between processes" (`cache_key.get`), and this component breaks that invariant.

**2. A rank that compiles while its peers loaded waits forever in sharded autotuning.** With `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning` (on by default), a compile of a program that spans processes splits its autotuning over them, and each process blocks in the coordination service's key-value store until the others' shares arrive. A rank that compiles alone waits for shares that never come. A one-device program never waits this way, because its compile takes `process_count` from its own devices.

The same hang happens in a real job. Stacks dumped at 150 s from a four-process training job with the cache on show every rank in `backend_compile_and_load`, in two different programs that both span the pool. Ranks 0 and 1 loaded the initial-state program from the cache and are compiling the train step. Ranks 2 and 3 missed the initial-state program and are compiling it. Each pair waits for autotuning shares of a program the other pair isn't compiling, and all four GPUs sit idle. A three-process trainer on GPUs 0-2 hung the same way in its first compile.

**Reproduction.** Plain `jax.distributed.initialize`, one process per GPU, with GPU1 (NVLink) and GPU2 (no NVLink) sharing one new cache directory. Each process compiles `local`, a matmul chain on its own GPU, then `pool`, the same chain over a batch split across both processes, and prints its topology fingerprint and each compile's key and hit or miss. `run.sh 1,2` runs it cold, then warm over the same directory, each run bounded to 150 s here.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
import logging
import os
import sys
import time

rank = int(sys.argv[1])
gpus = sys.argv[2].split(",")
os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = gpus[rank]
os.environ["JAX_ENABLE_COMPILATION_CACHE"] = "true"
os.environ["JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR"] = os.environ["REPRO_CACHE"]
os.environ["JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_MIN_COMPILE_TIME_SECS"] = "0"
os.environ["JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_MIN_ENTRY_SIZE_BYTES"] = "-1"

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from jax._src.lib import xla_client
from jax.sharding import NamedSharding, PartitionSpec as P


class Keys(logging.Handler):
    """Prints each compile's cache key and whether the persistent cache held it."""

    def emit(self, record):
        message = record.getMessage()
        if "cache hit for" in message or "CACHE MISS for" in message:
            module = message.split("'")[1]
            key = message.rsplit("'", 2)[-2]
            print(f"[{rank}] {'hit ' if 'hit for' in message else 'miss'} {module} key ...{key[-12:]}", flush=True)


logger = logging.getLogger("jax._src.compiler")
logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
logger.addHandler(Keys())
logger.propagate = False

jax.distributed.initialize(coordinator_address=f"127.0.0.1:{os.environ['REPRO_PORT']}",
                           num_processes=len(gpus), process_id=rank)
fingerprint = xla_client.get_topology_for_devices(jax.local_devices()).fingerprint()
print(f"[{rank}] GPU{gpus[rank]} topology fingerprint {fingerprint:016x}, jax {jax.__version__}", flush=True)


def local(x, w):
    for _ in range(6):
        x = jnp.tanh(x @ w)
    return jnp.sum(x)


def pool(x, w):
    for _ in range(6):
        x = jnp.tanh(x @ w)
    return jnp.sum(x)


began = time.perf_counter()
device = jax.local_devices()[0]
value = float(jax.jit(local)(jax.device_put(np.ones((2048, 1536), np.float32), device),
                             jax.device_put(np.eye(1536, dtype=np.float32) * 0.5, device)))
print(f"[{rank}] local ran in {time.perf_counter() - began:.1f}s: {value}", flush=True)

mesh = jax.make_mesh((jax.device_count(),), ("data",))
x = jax.make_array_from_process_local_data(NamedSharding(mesh, P("data")),
                                           np.ones((2048, 1536), np.float32) * (1 + rank))
w = jax.device_put(np.eye(1536, dtype=np.float32) * 0.5, NamedSharding(mesh, P()))
began = time.perf_counter()
value = float(jax.jit(pool)(x, w))
print(f"[{rank}] pool ran in {time.perf_counter() - began:.1f}s: {value}", flush=True)
```
</details>

<details><summary>run.sh</summary>

```bash
# run.sh <gpus> [python]: repro.py's cold run, then its warm run over the same new cache directory,
# one process per GPU of the comma-separated <gpus>, each run bounded to REPRO_SECONDS (240).
gpus=$1
python=${2:-python}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cache=$(mktemp -d "${REPRO_CACHE_ROOT:-/tmp}/repro-cache.XXXX")
count=$(echo "$gpus" | tr , '\n' | wc -l)
for run in cold warm; do
    port=$((20000 + RANDOM % 20000))
    began=$(date +%s)
    echo "== $run run over $cache"
    for ((rank = 0; rank < count; rank++)); do
        REPRO_CACHE=$cache REPRO_PORT=$port timeout -k 10 "${REPRO_SECONDS:-240}" "$python" "$here/repro.py" $rank "$gpus" 2>&1 \
            | grep -E "^\[[0-9]+\] " &
    done
    wait
    echo "== $run run took $(($(date +%s) - began)) s"
done
rm -rf "$cache"
```
</details>

Output with jax 0.11.2, `REPRO_SECONDS=150 bash run.sh 1,2`. In the warm run rank 0 loads `pool` and rank 1 misses it, and neither prints `pool ran` before the bound kills them:

```
== cold run over /workspace/scratch/dist-inference/repro-cache.gmSA
[1] GPU2 topology fingerprint d5bfe87ebbdab996, jax 0.11.2
[1] miss jit_local key ...f2ce2b8e3236
[1] local ran in 2.6s: 44397.05859375
[1] miss jit__identity_fn key ...cda6d34a8077
[1] miss jit_pool key ...c15ec8a6e12a
[1] pool ran in 0.6s: 114849.296875
[0] GPU1 topology fingerprint 2834ad2e578f5a6a, jax 0.11.2
[0] miss jit_local key ...e63b23ca61de
[0] local ran in 2.8s: 44397.05859375
[0] miss jit__identity_fn key ...dac62f07b528
[0] miss jit_pool key ...51c54fe47207
[0] pool ran in 0.6s: 114849.296875
== cold run took 7 s
== warm run over /workspace/scratch/dist-inference/repro-cache.gmSA
[1] GPU2 topology fingerprint d5bfe87ebbdab996, jax 0.11.2
[1] miss jit_local key ...f2ce2b8e3236
[1] local ran in 0.6s: 44397.05859375
[1] miss jit__identity_fn key ...cda6d34a8077
[1] miss jit_pool key ...c15ec8a6e12a
[0] GPU1 topology fingerprint 2834ad2e578f5a6a, jax 0.11.2
[0] hit  jit_local key ...e63b23ca61de
[0] local ran in 0.1s: 44397.05859375
[0] hit  jit__identity_fn key ...dac62f07b528
[0] hit  jit_pool key ...51c54fe47207
== warm run took 160 s
```

The same program on GPUs 0,1 or 2,3, whose processes fingerprint alike, runs warm on both processes. A smaller program doesn't always hang: in one jitted step of four 1024x1024 bf16 matmuls on GPUs 1,2, the rank that missed compiled alone and finished. Its keys differed the same way.

**Expected.** One cache decision per computation: every process of it loads, or every process compiles, so `jax_share_binary_between_hosts` also keeps working on hosts like this. Separately, sharded autotuning could fail after a bounded wait with an error that names the missing shares, rather than hang.

**Proposed fix**, carried on AshishKumar4/jax branch `cache-key-pool-fingerprints` (0afcd84c, on main), with a 0.11.2 carry on `v0.11.2-cache-key-pool-fingerprints` (19a48d1d):

- Each process publishes, once through the distributed runtime client, its topology fingerprint and its accelerators: platform and runtime version, the CUDA driver, cuDNN and cuBLAS versions, and each local device's kind, compute capability and core count. It reads each peer's once.
- For a computation that spans processes, if every process names the same accelerators, `_hash_accelerator_config` hashes the sorted set of their fingerprints, so every process computes one key. Links don't change an executable that spans processes: at this XLA revision `active_links` reaches compilation only through the SOL latency estimator (Hopper, Blackwell and MI300), the analytical estimator (off by default) and the collective kernels (every replica local to one process).
- If the processes name different accelerators, the computation gets no key. `_get_cache_key` already turns that into compiling without the cache on every process, and it logs which processes have which accelerators. Sharing would load code built for another GPU.

With it, the same `run.sh 1,2` gives one key on both ranks, and the warm run loads it on both:

```
== warm run over /workspace/scratch/dist-inference/repro-cache.ztBX
[0] GPU1 topology fingerprint 2834ad2e578f5a6a, jax 0.11.2.post3
[0] hit  jit_local key ...e63b23ca61de
[0] local ran in 0.1s: 44397.05859375
[0] hit  jit__identity_fn key ...eaec7e237ec8
[0] hit  jit_pool key ...b63357934d79
[0] pool ran in 0.0s: 114849.296875
[1] GPU2 topology fingerprint d5bfe87ebbdab996, jax 0.11.2.post3
[1] miss jit_local key ...f2ce2b8e3236
[1] local ran in 0.6s: 44397.05859375
[1] hit  jit__identity_fn key ...eaec7e237ec8
[1] hit  jit_pool key ...b63357934d79
[1] pool ran in 0.0s: 114849.296875
== warm run took 3 s
```

`jit_local` runs on one process, so it keeps its per-process key, and only process 0 writes it. Rank 1 recompiling it is harmless: a one-device compile doesn't shard its autotuning.

The four-process training job gives the same picture with the fix. Every program that spans the pool loads on every process, and the warm start reaches its first step in 14.2 s against 69.3 s cold. Two processes of two GPUs each take 13.0 s against 63.0 s, and GPUs 1,2 take 13.5 s against 63.5 s. Processes whose fingerprint differs from process 0's still compile their few one-process programs, as rank 1 does `jit_local` above.

Coverage:

| Case | Key with the fix | How it was checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processes that differ only in links (this issue) | one key per computation | this repro on GPUs 1,2 and 0,3, and on 4 processes over GPUs 0-3: warm loads everywhere; unit tests with fake fingerprints |
| Processes on different accelerators (architecture, runtime, driver, cuDNN, cuBLAS, kind, cores) | no key; compiled without the cache on every process, logged | unit tests with fake records; not on hardware |
| Processes whose fingerprints differ only in fields not in the accelerators string (clocks, memory, ECC, CUB, toolkit) | shared | not covered: a residual, bounded by `GpuDeviceInfoProto`'s fields |
| Processes that fingerprint alike (a homogeneous GPU cluster) | unchanged: a one-element set hashes the same 8 bytes | GPUs 0,1 and 2,3 give the same key as jax 0.11.2; unit test |
| A single process, or no distributed client (e.g. single controller) | unchanged: the old path | same hash as jax 0.11.2 on an RTX 3090 (1 and 4 devices), on CPU, and on a TPU v6e (1 chip) |
| TPU multi-host slice | unchanged if every host's fingerprint is the same | unverified: the TPU client's topology code isn't public |
| Cost | one publish per process and one read per peer, per distributed client | unit test |

Workarounds: `JAX_ENABLE_COMPILATION_CACHE=false` for multi-process GPU jobs. `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false` ends the wait, but then ranks can run different executables (loaded on some, freshly autotuned on others), which is openxla/xla#7716's deadlock.

Related: openxla/xla#49371 (the XLA side: the GPU topology fingerprint hashes one local device's links), #33852 (a rare hang with one process stuck compiling while the others wait at the next sync; this mechanism would produce that picture), marin-community/marin#9042 (the same wait in XLA's autotuner when ranks lower different HLO), openxla/xla#7716, openxla/xla#40177.

### System info (python version, jaxlib version, accelerator, etc.)

```
jax:    0.11.2
jaxlib: 0.11.2
numpy:  2.5.3
python: 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0]
process_count: 1 (the repro runs one process per GPU through jax.distributed.initialize)
platform: Linux 5.15.0-191-generic x86_64

$ nvidia-smi
NVIDIA-SMI 595.84    Driver Version: 595.84    CUDA Version: 13.3
GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, 00000000:02:00.0, 24576MiB
GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, 00000000:03:00.0, 24576MiB
GPU 2: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, 00000000:83:00.0, 24576MiB
GPU 3: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, 00000000:84:00.0, 24576MiB

$ nvidia-smi topo -m
GPU0-GPU1 NV4, GPU2-GPU3 PHB, GPU0/1-GPU2/3 SYS

jax-cuda12-plugin 0.11.2; jax._src.lib.cuda_versions: runtime 12090, driver 13030, cuDNN 92501, cuBLAS 120902
```

issue.title: Multi-process GPU: the processes of one computation compute different persistent-cache keys when only some GPUs have NVLink, and a warm run hangs in sharded autotuning
